title: Intrinsically disordered regions in the transcription factor MYC:MAX modulate DNA binding via intramolecular interactions
authors: Stefan Schütz; Christian Bergsdorf; Sandra Hänni-Holzinger; Andreas Lingel; Martin Renatus; Alvar D. Gossert; Wolfgang Jahnke
one_liner_zh: 该文通过NMR和SPR研究MYC:MAX转录因子内部无序区与DNA结合域间的分子内互作对DNA结合的调控，虽聚焦TF-DNA体系但方法以实验为主，缺乏AI或物理模拟建模，故评分为6。
abstract: The basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) transcription factor (TF) MYC is in large parts an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein. In complex with its obligate heterodimerization partner MAX, MYC preferentially binds E-Box DNA sequences (CANNTG). At promotors containing these sequence motifs, MYC controls fundamental cellular processes such as cell cycle progression, metabolism, and apoptosis. A vast network of proteins controls MYC function via intermolecular interactions. In this work, we establish another layer of MYC regulation by intramolecular interactions. We use Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy to identify and map multiple binding sites for the C-terminal MYC:MAX DNA binding domain (DBD) on the intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) in the MYC N-terminus. We find that these binding events in trans are driven by electrostatic attraction, that they have distinct affinities, and that they are competitive with DNA binding. Thereby, we observe the strongest effects for the N-terminal MYC box 0 (Mb0), a conserved motif involved in MYC transactivation and target gene induction. We prepared recombinant full-length MYC:MAX complex and demonstrate that the interactions identified in this work are also relevant in cis , i.e. as intramolecular interactions. These findings are supported by Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) experiments, which revealed that intramolecular IDR:DBD interactions in MYC decelerate the association of MYC:MAX complexes to DNA. Our work offers new insights how bHLH-LZ TFs are regulated by intramolecular interactions, which opens up new possibilities for drug discovery.
abstract_zh: 基础螺旋-环-螺旋亮氨酸拉链（bHLH-LZ）转录因子（TF）MYC在很大程度上是一种内在无序的致癌蛋白。与其专性异二聚化伙伴MAX形成复合物后，MYC优先结合E-Box DNA序列（CANNTG）。在含有这些序列基序的启动子上，MYC调控细胞周期进程、代谢和凋亡等基本细胞过程。一个庞大的蛋白质网络通过分子间相互作用调控MYC功能。在本工作中，我们通过分子内相互作用建立了MYC调控的另一层面。我们利用核磁共振（NMR）波谱学鉴定并绘制了C端MYC:MAX DNA结合域（DBD）在MYC N端内在无序区域（IDRs）上的多个结合位点。我们发现这些反式结合事件由静电吸引驱动，具有不同的亲和力，并且与DNA结合存在竞争性。由此，我们观察到N端MYC box 0（Mb0）效应最强，这是一个参与MYC反式激活和靶基因诱导的保守基序。我们制备了重组全长MYC:MAX复合物，并证明本工作中鉴定的相互作用在顺式条件下同样相关，即作为分子内相互作用。这些发现得到表面等离子体共振（SPR）实验的支持，该实验揭示MYC中分子内IDR:DBD相互作用减慢了MYC:MAX复合物与DNA的结合。我们的工作为bHLH-LZ转录因子如何通过分子内相互作用调控提供了新见解，这为药物发现开辟了新可能性。
